title: Structure, dynamics, and function of SrnR, a transcription factor for nickel-dependent gene expression.
authors: Mazzei, Luca; Musiani, Francesco; Zerko, Szymon; Kozminski, Wiktor; Cianci, Michele; Beniamino, Ylenia; Ciurli, Stefano; Zambelli, Barbara
one_liner_zh: 该文通过X射线晶体学、NMR、原子级分子动力学模拟和分子对接，综合解析了镍依赖性转录因子SrnR的结构、动态及其与DNA操纵子的两步结合机制，属于典型的TF-DNA互作机制建模研究。
abstract: Streptomyces griseus, a bacterium producing antibacterial drugs and featuring possible application in phytoremediation, expresses two metal-dependent superoxide dismutase (SOD) enzymes, containing either Fe(II) or Ni(II) in their active site. In particular, the alternative expression of the two proteins occurs in a metal-dependent mode, with the Fe(II)-enzyme gene (sodF) repressed at high intracellular Ni(II) concentrations by a two-component system (TCS). This complex involves two proteins, namely SgSrnR and SgSrnQ, which represent the transcriptional regulator and the Ni(II) sensor of the system, respectively. SgSrnR belongs to the ArsR/SmtB family of metal-dependent transcription factors; in the apo-form and in the absence of SgSrnQ, it can bind the DNA operator of sodF, upregulating gene transcription. According to a recently proposed hypothesis, Ni(II) binding to SgSrnQ would promote its interaction with SgSrnR, causing the release of the complex from DNA and the consequent downregulation of the sodF expression. SgSrnQ is predicted to be highly disordered, thus the understanding, at the molecular level, of how the SgSrnR/SgSrnQ TCS specifically responds to Ni(II) requires the knowledge of the structural, dynamic, and functional features of SgSrnR. These were investigated synergistically in this work using X-ray crystallography, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, atomistic molecular dynamics calculations, isothermal titration calorimetry, and in silico molecular docking. The results reveal that the homodimeric apo-SgSrnR binds to its operator in a two-step process that involves the more rigid globular portion of the protein and leaves its largely disordered regions available to possibly interact with the disordered SgSrnQ in a Ni-dependent process.
abstract_zh: 灰色链霉菌（*Streptomyces griseus*）是一种产生抗菌药物并可能在植物修复中具有应用前景的细菌，其表达两种金属依赖性超氧化物歧化酶（SOD），活性位点分别含有Fe(II)或Ni(II)。特别地，这两种蛋白的交替表达以金属依赖性模式发生，其中Fe(II)酶基因（*sodF*）在细胞内高Ni(II)浓度下被双组分系统（TCS）抑制。该复合物涉及两种蛋白，即SgSrnR和SgSrnQ，分别代表系统的转录调控因子和Ni(II)传感器。SgSrnR属于ArsR/SmtB家族的金属依赖性转录因子；在脱辅基形式且无SgSrnQ存在时，它能结合*sodF*的DNA操纵区，上调基因转录。根据最近提出的假说，Ni(II)与SgSrnQ结合会促进其与SgSrnR的相互作用，导致复合物从DNA上释放，进而下调*sodF*表达。预测SgSrnQ高度无序，因此，要在分子水平上理解SgSrnR/SgSrnQ TCS如何特异性响应Ni(II)，需了解SgSrnR的结构、动态和功能特征。本研究通过X射线晶体学、核磁共振（NMR）波谱学、原子级分子动力学计算、等温滴定量热法和计算机模拟分子对接协同探究了这些特征。结果表明，同源二聚体的脱辅基SgSrnR以两步过程结合其操纵区，该过程涉及蛋白中较刚性的球状部分，并使其大部分无序区域保持可用，以便在Ni依赖性过程中可能与无序的SgSrnQ相互作用。
